div.p: In the rapidly evolving landscape of real-time systems, particularly autonomous-driving technologies, directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) have emerged as an essential model for delineating task dependencies and facilitating parallel processing. This growing complexity and computational demand are making it increasingly challenging to efficiently schedule tasks on multicore processors. Among various DAG scheduling algorithms, federated scheduling stands out for its efficacy in managing tasks with implicit deadlines. However, it comes at the cost of potentially over-consuming core resources and diminishing the overall schedulability of task set. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid scheduling method tailored for sporadic DAG tasks, which integrates principles from bundled scheduling to optimize core utilization and enhance system schedulability.

div.head: I. INTRODUCTION
div.p: The advancement of real-time systems, exemplified by autonomous-driving technologies, has led to escalating computational requirements that are straining traditional processor architectures [1]. To address this computational bottleneck, multi-core processors have come into the spotlight as an effective solution [2]. Within this context, directed acyclic graphs (DAGs) serve as a key representation model that captures task dependencies and enables parallel execution [3], [4], becoming indispensable for the management of complex tasks inherent in modern real-time systems like autonomousdriving [4]- [16].

Building on the crucial role of DAGs in managing these complex tasks, one commonly employed metric for evaluating the efficacy of different scheduling algorithms is the capacity augmentation bound [5]. This metric is contingent on the total utilization of the task set and the ratio of the critical path length to the deadline for each task, and serves as a simple scheduleability test. Federated scheduling is considered to be an effective scheduling algorithm with excellent capacity augmentation bound for DAG tasks with implicit deadlines [4]. However, federated scheduling may require excessive cores depending on the ratio of critical path length and deadline [9], which is a condition for capacity augmentation bound, and the schedulability of the entire task set may be greatly reduced. There are various approaches to remedy this problem [9], [16], but these approaches do not focus on the idle time that occurs in the dedicated cores allocated.

To address the limitations associated with federated scheduling, particularly its tendency to over-allocate cores and neglect idle time, this paper proposes a hybrid scheduling method that combines federated scheduling with bundled scheduling [7].

Unlike traditional gang scheduling [17], where parallel threads are grouped into "gangs" for collective execution, bundled scheduling adopts a more flexible model. Specifically, it reserves only the number of cores actually needed for each computational node, leading to more efficient CPU utilization when compared to well-known gang task models like the rigid model [18]. The proposed method aims to enhance system schedulability by judiciously applying bundled scheduling to tasks. We target tasks that have smaller critical path lengthto-deadline ratios and exhibit larger idle times when allocated dedicated cores, all within the framework of capacity augmentation bound conditions.
The contributions of this paper:

• One of the problems in conventional federated scheduling is the excessive core requests from tasks with a low ratio between critical path length and deadline, which our method aims to avoid. • The integration of bundle-based scheduling enables the consideration of low-utilization tasks, hence enhancing schedulability. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section II describes a system model. Section III introduces the proposed scheduling method and a positive example of the proposed method. The conclusions and suggestions for future work are presented in Section IV.

div.head: II. SYSTEM MODEL AND BACKGROUND
div.p: This section introduces the system and task models considered. In addition, we describe federated scheduling and bundled scheduling, both of which provide the basis for the proposed scheduling approach.

div.head: A. System Model
div.p: We focus on a multi-core processor system equipped with m homogeneous cores. Define a sporadic parallel task set τ consisting of n tasks with τ = {τ 1 , τ 2 , . . ., τ n }. Jobs are instances of these tasks and are released sporadically. For a task τ i , T i is the minimum arrival time, which is the time interval between consecutive releases of jobs from task. D i specifies the relative deadline of τ i , and we focus on tasks with implicit deadlines, where T i = D i . When a job originating from task τ i arrives at time t, it must be completed by the absolute deadline of t + D i , and the next job from τ i cannot be released earlier than t + T i . Each task τ i is characterized by a graph
div.formula: G i = (V i , E i ). V i is the set of nodes (v i,1 , v i,2 , . . ., v i,s
div.p: ), each with worst-case execution time (WCET) c(v i,j ). Let E i be a set of edges, each of which is denoted by (v i,j , v i,k ) ∈ E i . The edges represent node dependencies, meaning that the execution of node v i,k cannot start execution until node v i,j has finished. The total execution time C i of task τ i is the sum of WCETs c(v i,j ) of all nodes in task τ i . The critical path length L i for task τ i is defined as the time required to execute τ i when an unlimited number of cores are available. The utilization u i of task τ i can be expressed as Ci Ti = Ci Di , and the total utilization U of the entire task set is obtained by U = τi∈τ u i . A scheduler provides a capacity augmentation bound of b if it can schedule any task set τ that satisfies the following two conditions: (1) the total utilization U of τ is no greater than m b , and (2) the worst-case critical-path length of each task L i is no more than Di b [5].

div.head: B. Federated Scheduling
div.p: Federated scheduling [4] is an effective approach for managing diverse types of tasks, separating them into highutilization and low-utilization categories. High-utilization tasks τ high (u i > 1) are allocated to dedicated cores and executed to complete processing by the deadline. The number of cores n i allocated to high-utilization tasks is obtained by the following equation [4]:
div.formula: n i = C i -L i D i -L i . (1
div.p: Using a work-conserving scheduler ensures that all jobs within the high-utilization task can meet their deadlines. In contrast, low-utilization tasks τ low (u i ≤ 1), are treated as regular sequential tasks. These tasks are scheduled on the remaining available processors, denoted by m low , which is calculated as m-τi∈τhigh n i . Low-utilization tasks are scheduled for the remaining processors by traditional multiprocessor scheduling algorithms (e.g., global EDF or partitioned EDF). If m low is negative (m ≤ τi∈τhigh n i ), the task set is considered unschedulable.

A significant drawback of federated scheduling is its potential to over-allocate cores, particularly when the ratio of the critical path length L i to the execution deadline D i of a high-utilization task τ i is small. For example, consider task τ i , with a total execution time C i = 16 and the critical path length L i = 4. Assuming that the minimum arrival time T i (= D i ) = 6, task τ i qualifies as a high-utilization task because the utilization rate u i is Ci Ti = 16 6 > 1. Using Eq. This results in excessive core allocation relative to the task's actual utilization rate. In addition, federated scheduling tends to waste substantial resources. Each task operates exclusively on its designated cores, with unused processing capacity that cannot be harnessed by other tasks.

div.head: C. Bundled Scheduling
div.p: In bundled scheduling [7], each DAG task τ i is assigned a bundled task model. For example, consider the DAG shown in Fig. 1. If [t, t ] is the interval that uses a constant number of cores h i,j as a result of the simulation, assign a bundle of length l i,j = t -t and height h i,j for each maximum interval. An example of the bundled task assigned in the m = 4 case in Fig. 2. Note that the parallelism of the DAG in Fig. 1 might exceed m.

For each node v i,k , record its starting and ending indices within the bundle, denoted τ start i,k and τ end i,k , respectively. For τ start i,k ≤ j and τ end i,k ≥ j, then node v i,k is assigned to bundle τ i,j . Finally, for each node v i,k , let t start i,k denote the start time of execution relative to the start time of τ start i,k . The actual execution follows the rules proven in Lemma 1 of Ref. [7].

Bundled tasks are scheduled according to a global preemptive fixed priority scheduling scheme. The bundles τ i,j awaiting execution are sorted in descending priority order. A bundle is executed if its height h i,j is smaller than the number of remaining available cores. One issue with bundled scheduling lies in the frequent occurrence of interference among statically assigned bundles. This interference stems from the inherent structure of the bundle model, potentially rendering the scheduling infeasible. An illustrative example of this issue is presented in Section III-B.

div.head: III. PROPOSED METHOD
div.p: In this section, the proposed scheduling method is described in detail. In addition, we show an example where the proposed method outperforms existing scheduling algorithms.

div.head: A. Scheduling Strategy
div.p: The proposed employs bundled-based scheduling to solve the problem of federated scheduling, i.e., excessive core requests when the difference between the critical path length and deadline of a task is small. By assigning bundled scheduling to tasks with small differences between critical path lengths and deadlines, excessive core requests are avoided. Furthermore, since bundled scheduling does not assign dedicated cores, it can also consider low-utilization tasks.
Given a task set, our proposed method performs scheduling in four steps.

• All tasks are executed in federated scheduling if the task set τ satisfies the following two conditions based on the capacity augmentation bound [5]: (1) the total utilization U of τ is no greater than m b , and (2) the worst-case critical-path length of each task L i is no more than Di b . • In the case of a task set that does not satisfy either of these conditions, tasks are divided into two disjoint sets: high-utilization tasks τ high (u i > 1) and low-utilization tasks τ low (u i ≤ 1). Among high-utilization tasks τ high , let τ F be the tasks with L i ≤ Di b and τ B be the tasks with L i > Di b . • The tasks of ∀τ i ∈ τ F are executed by federated scheduling, using Eq. ( 1) to determine the required number of dedicated cores n i . • The tasks of ∀τ i ∈ τ B are converted to bundled tasks that use the number of cores m B = m -τi∈τF n i . div.head: IV. CONCLUSION
div.p: In this paper, we proposed a hybrid scheduling method that employs techniques based on bundled scheduling for sporadic DAG tasks. The proposed method enhances schedulability compared to existing methods by minimizing excessive core requests and accounting for low-utilization tasks. Future work includes refining research, developing improved equations for assigning tasks to appropriate scheduling algorithms, and investigating methods for handling constrained or arbitrarydeadline tasks.
